p01.why: Each reference added to a reference type collapses as DCL-4 gives, and const on a reference alias has no effect, so every assertion holds.

p02.why: The lvalues reach sink(int&) and the prvalue and xvalue reach sink(int&&), so calls is 1+10+1+10 = 22.

p03.why: Mix<Part> lists Part twice in its bases.

p04.why: For an empty pack the using-declaration declares nothing, so f(1) picks f(double); with Small, f(int) is the better match.

p05.why: Each base gets one member initializer from the expansion, so the members hold 4, 4, 1, and 2.

p06.why: A function parameter pack, here from auto..., must not have a default argument.

p07.why: The member template packs expand the outer pack, and both lists have two elements.

p08.why: sizeof... works on each kind of pack, gives a constant of the type of sizeof, and counts the init capture pack too.

p09.why: T is const int&, so the cast gives an lvalue and decltype of the parenthesized cast is const int&.

p10.why: The mem_init value(x)... names a data member, which must not be expanded.

p11.why: The operand of sizeof... must be a pack name in parentheses, and T* is a pattern.

p12.why: Pair<A, B>... expands A with two elements and B with one element.

p13.why: L<T..., U> is a non-deduced position, U and T come from the other arguments, and the match then checks the first list.

p14.why: An expansion can give arguments to the fixed parameters of a class template.

p15.why: The type of a function parameter pack must name a template parameter pack or hold auto, and int does neither.

p16.why: An expansion must not give an argument to a non-pack parameter of an alias template.

p17.why: decltype(x) is int&, int&&, int&&, so the casts give an lvalue and two xvalues.

p18.why: f<void> forms a void parameter, so substitution fails and f(...) is chosen; f<int>(1) prefers the exact match.

p19.why: [=, x...] repeats the mode of the capture default.

p20.why: The expansion gives Part twice in the base list.

p21.why: T is not a pack, so T... with no name is the variable argument part; the other two are real packs.

p22.why: Inside the class, f finds a using-declarator expanded over an empty pack; PACK-30 needs no diagnostic, GCC and EDG call ::f, and Clang rejects.

p23.why: s.bits is a const bit-field, so T is const int& and the reference binds to a temporary; PACK-31 forbids only non-const bit-fields.

p24.why: c{p...} declares one capture that is not a pack, and with one element it is an int.

p25.why: The fold uses up the pack N, so the outer ... has no pack in its pattern.

p26.why: A non-const lvalue bit-field is passed to a forwarding reference.

p27.why: Different lengths in the return type remove the template, so zip(...) gives 2; equal lengths give List<Pair<int, char>>.

p28.why: Call<void> makes run have a parameter of type void through the expansion.

p29.why: Each using-declarator names the member, operator, or constructors of every base, so each call finds its own overload.

p30.why: Every declarator form is a valid function parameter pack, and the default argument sits before the pack.

p31.why: References from a template argument, an alias, and decltype collapse as DCL-4 gives.

p32.why: D<A> finds A::f, but D<> uses f found through an empty using-declarator expansion; GCC and EDG give 2, Clang rejects.

p33.why: On a member, alignas(T...) takes the strictest alignment, and an empty expansion adds no requirement.

p34.why: sizeof... gives a constant usable as a template argument and an array bound.

p35.why: List<Ts..., int> is non-deduced, Ts is the explicit char, and the parameter type List<char, int> matches the argument.

p36.why: An empty expansion leaves int(), Point{}, count(), and a class with no bases.

p37.why: sizeof... counts as an inner expansion, so the outer pattern holds no pack.

p38.why: x... copies, &x... references, and each capture default with a pack capture of the other mode is valid.

p39.why: The pattern x holds no pack.

p40.why: The inner expansion takes the inner T, the outer one the rest, and one pack can be expanded in both.

p41.why: Each copy is one argument or one element, and a braced list is evaluated from left to right.

p42.why: T... before int in a function type is non-deduced; with T deduced as empty, Clang and GCC fail deduction and pick take(...); the specification records that EDG differs but not how.

p43.why: On a class, GCC takes the alignment of the last element (2) and fails the assertion; Clang and EDG take 8.

p44.why: Each alias expands its pack into List, and the member alias template zips two packs of equal length.

p45.why: An unnamed pack must not have its ... inside parentheses.

p46.why: Each copy of the pattern gets its own closure, and the comma fold runs from left to right: 1*5 + 2*7 = 19.

p47.why: The outer pack has two elements and Shaped gets one template.

p48.why: Braced-list elements run in order, giving 1, 3, 6; the two expansions give six arguments.

p49.why: A mem_init that names a data member is expanded.

p50.why: [&, &x...] repeats the mode of the capture default.

p51.why: y is a pack in the body and is used outside any expansion.

p52.why: x has a name, so ... is the variable argument part and the pack T stays unexpanded.

p53.why: The operand of sizeof... needs parentheses.

p54.why: [=] copies each element of p before the reset, and [&] sees the reset to 0.

p55.why: Ts... is non-deduced, so Ts is empty and List<int> does not match List<char, int>; no viable function.

p56.why: A pack of references to arrays and a trailing pack after a plain parameter are both valid.

p57.why: Init capture packs copy or reference each element, and an empty one declares nothing.

p58.why: The base list order sets the base initialization order, so the log is 12 and 21.

p59.why: int{} is 0, count(1) is chosen for the empty pack, and Wrap<> is List<>.

p60.why: Each element deduces on its own: int&, const int&, int, int.

p61.why: U... belongs to the inner expansion and T to the outer one.

p62.why: T is not a pack, so it cannot be the operand of sizeof....

p63.why: auto x... is one parameter followed by the variable argument part, so sizeof(x) is that of the first argument.

p64.why: Three<0, N...> gives the expansion to fixed constant parameters.

p65.why: Only a function or template parameter can have ... in its declarator.

p66.why: A function parameter pack must not have a default argument.

p67.why: An expansion for non-pack concept parameters: Clang and GCC reject, EDG accepts.

p68.why: x is a pack used outside any expansion.
